assertions: Ingests the input via `jira issue view PROJ-482 --json` (or equivalent) before any other phase work
Spawns an Explore/haiku discovery agent to map the project's stack and commands before assessing complexity
Computes a complexity score from the signals table and proposes a team mode via AskUserQuestion before spawning any implementation agents
Creates `.specs/<short-id>/` with input-digest.md and README.md before writing or editing any source code

If full mode is used, spawns roles by the names in the rewritten catalog (e.g. product-lead, architect, adversary-reviewer, an implementation-engineer per component) rather than the old product-manager/scrum-master/frontend-dev/backend-dev split, and never calls a `Teammate` tool or operation that doesn't exist in this environment's actual tool surface
Does not modify any source code before the user approval gate is passed

evals.prompt: /team-implement Add a real-time collaborative comment system to the docs editor — needs a websocket backend, new DB tables for comment threads, and a React panel; two prior attempts got the sync logic wrong
assertions: Runs Phase 0 discovery/complexity assessment before Phase 1 clarifying questions
Asks clarifying questions via AskUserQuestion to resolve scope/tech ambiguities before drafting the spec

Spawns (or, in a sequential fallback, runs the same prompt as) an Adversary Reviewer against the spec/design artifacts and gates progress on zero BLOCKER findings or a max of 2 revision cycles before task decomposition
Presents the full plan via AskUserQuestion at the approval gate before Phase 6 implementation begins
Enforces separate, explicitly-stated file-scope boundaries between the frontend and backend implementation engineers during Phase 6 (no engineer edits a file outside its declared scope)

evals.prompt: /team-implement Draft a full spec for migrating our REST API to GraphQL, but don't write any code yet — I just want the plan reviewed first
assertions: Completes planning phases (0-5) without editing or creating any application source files
Presents the approval gate with a 'Save spec only — do not implement' option among the choices
When spec-only is selected, skips directly to Phase 9 teardown without spawning any implementation engineer
Spec artifacts exist under `.specs/<short-id>/` (e.g. brief/design/tasks files, or their full-mode equivalents) before the session ends
No source code files are modified at any point in the transcript, and no destructive or mutating shell command (git commit, rm, migration apply, package install) is ever run

evals.prompt: /team-implement Rebuild the checkout flow across the web frontend, the payments backend, and a new fraud-detection service — this touches three components and handles payment data, so it needs a real team
assertions: Complexity assessment scores this at or near the full-mode threshold (3+ components, security-sensitive payment data) and recommends or proposes full mode

If `CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS` is unset or a `Task ... team_name` call fails, the run falls back to Lite mode (sequential Task subagents, no cross-agent SendMessage) rather than stalling, erroring out, or inventing a `Teammate` tool call

The fallback is stated to the user (not silently swapped) and the same phase → gate → phase structure (clarify → spec → design → adversarial review → tasks → approval gate) is still followed in Lite mode
No code is written before the user approval gate passes, in either mode
Every tool call the transcript shows spawning or coordinating an agent uses a tool that actually exists in this environment's surface — never a fabricated `Teammate({...})` call
